prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: Topological insulators remain my first choice after reading all eight ballots. Seven of eight members ranked B028, five of them in the top three, so support is broad across subfields and not only from theorists. The discovery is a complete chain from idea to observation: Kane and Mele's Z2 classification and quantum spin Hall proposal, then Molenkamp's unambiguous HgTe edge-channel measurement. It has been confirmed over fifteen to twenty years in many materials and techniques, the interpretation is stable, and the concept now shapes materials theory, photonics and device thinking. Of the shortlist, it pairs the cleanest conceptual originality with the longest independent confirmation, and the case for recognition now is strong.
statement.case_against: The credit is the weak point. The names supplied omit Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, whose HgTe proposal directly enabled Molenkamp's experiment, and Fu, Moore and Balents for the three-dimensional theory. Choosing Mele over Hasan, or the reverse, is a judgement about 2D versus 3D that I cannot settle from the supplied record. The 2016 prize on topological phases may also be read as having already covered much of this ground, which a committee could weigh against it.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B028 first but proposes Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, giving the three-dimensional ARPES identification a slot ahead of Mele, and he stresses that the 2016 overlap is real but not disqualifying.
responses.response: I agree on the 2016 point: Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz honoured topological phase transitions and the quantum Hall precursors, not the Z2 classification or time-reversal-protected edge and surface states. I disagree on dropping Mele. The Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall proposal are a joint Kane-Mele result, and without them neither the HgTe experiment nor the 3D work has a framework. Hasan's ARPES work is decisive for 3D, but with three places the theory pair and the first experiment give the most coherent single citation. I would accept Hasan only if the committee decides the prize should explicitly cover the 3D branch, and that would cost a theory slot.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B034 first, calling the optical lattice clock a clear, durable measurement advance with a clean two-person credit, and ranks B028 only fourth as outside his specialty.
responses.response: I accept the credit for B034 is cleaner than for any other shortlisted candidate: Katori and Ye map directly onto proposal and realisation. That is why I keep it as an alternative. But a clean attribution is not greater scientific merit, and B028 created a new class of quantum matter, where B034 is an advance in precision of an established technique. Your own flagged link to the Ye-Hall environment is worth noting, and Ye's frequency-comb work overlaps with the 2005 prize, which Mehlig also raised. I would ask whether that overlap weakens the novelty claim for B034 relative to B028.

responses.point: Mehlig puts B046 first with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Andrei, and sees B028 as mature and overdue but weakened by the 2016 prize and the unresolved allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and uncredited theorists.
responses.response: The allocation difficulty you describe for B028 is real, and I flagged it myself. But B046 has the same problem in a sharper form, with four credited names for three slots, an Andrei versus Bistritzer choice and a pairing mechanism still unresolved. B046 is about seven years old, while B028 has two decades of confirmation, so I regard B046 as the stronger candidate for a later year, not this one. I would back it as the second alternative if B028 stalls on credit.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B046 first and treats it as a rare case in which a band-structure prediction preceded and guided a field-defining experiment, while B028 at second is for him exceptional and arguably overdue.
responses.response: I share your admiration for the theory-then-experiment arc of B046, and the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is a beautiful piece of work. But the same arc holds for B028, where the prediction came in 2005 and the experiment in 2007, and in B028 the pairing-mechanism type of open question does not hang over the claim. Your suggested subset of Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan is defensible, but I still prefer Mele to Hasan for the reason given to Danielsson.

uncertainties: Whether the committee wants the prize to cover the 3D topological insulator branch (Hasan) at the cost of Mele, or the 2D theory-plus-experiment story.
Contributions of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Balents cannot be accommodated by the supplied names, and I have not verified priority details beyond my own recollection.
How much weight the 2016 topological-phases prize should carry against B028.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal issue for B028 is apparent from my profile; Chalmers and WACQT have no documented link to the topological-insulator candidates. I would disclose that my Chalmers and WACQT ties are to superconducting-circuit work and to Chalmers colleagues associated with the 2025 prize, which would matter only if circuit QED (B035) were discussed, and that candidate is not on this shortlist.
